deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a 'dérivateur' D in Grothendieck's sense, with cohomological conventions. For a category I, D(I) holds coefficient systems on I. For f: I→J there is f^* with right adjoint f_* (cohomology). H_D(I,ξ) means p_{I*}ξ, where p_I: I→e.

Shapes:
- Ψ is the span shape 0→a, 0→b.
- Q = Δ^1×Δ^1 is the square, and K: Ψ→Q is the inclusion of three corners (0↦(0,0), a↦(0,1), b↦(1,0)).

A diagram X_0→X_a, X_0→X_b in Cat of type Ψ defines, by the Grothendieck construction, a category 𝒳 cofibred over Ψ, with projection φ: 𝒳→Ψ. Up to weak equivalence 𝒳 is the homotopy pushout (hocolim) of the span.

Construction (finishing the 'Principe (P)' begun on p.47). For ξ ∈ D(𝒳), set γ_0 = φ_*ξ ∈ D(Ψ) and γ = K_*γ_0 ∈ D(Q). Then:
- γ(1,1) ≃ H_D(𝒳,ξ), by transitivity of p_*.
- γ(0,0), γ(0,1), γ(1,0) ≃ H_D(X_0,ξ), H_D(X_a,ξ), H_D(X_b,ξ).
The last identifications use cofibredness. The value of φ_* at i is the cohomology of the preimage 𝒳_{/i} = φ^{-1}(Ψ_{/i}). Since the fibre X_i ↪ 𝒳_{/i} has an adjoint (push along cocartesian arrows), it is a homotopy equivalence and does not change cohomology.

The NB addresses a subtlety. In 𝒳 the fibres X_a, X_b are disjoint, so the square of categories X_0→X_a→𝒳, X_0→X_b→𝒳 commutes only up to the natural transformation x→f(x). The square of strict inclusions 𝒳_{/0} ⊂ 𝒳_{/a}, 𝒳_{/b} ⊂ 𝒳, however, does commute. The cohomology square (*), with H(𝒳) at the top, H(X_a) and H(X_b) in the middle and H(X_0) at the bottom, is obtained from that commuting square by applying H_D(−,ξ).

By construction γ is cartesian: it is right Kan extended from the span, i.e. a homotopy pullback. This gives H(𝒳) ≃ H(X_a) ×^h_{H(X_0)} H(X_b), an abstract Mayer–Vietoris statement valid in any derivator. Grothendieck remarks this would hold for any 𝒳 'propre' over Ψ, not only cofibred ones.

He then expects that cofibredness should also give that γ is COcartesian. He judges this not deducible from Der 1–Der 5, 5'. So he adds a provisional axiom 'Der 6': if 𝒳 is cofibred over Ψ and ξ ∈ D(𝒳), then K_*φ_*ξ ∈ D(Δ^1×Δ^1) is cartesian and also cocartesian. A marginal heading reads 'Axiome des cofibrations'.

On the next page he dualises this to Der 6' (fibred categories, φ_!). He notes that Der 6' for D does not give Der 6 for the dual D°. He then replaces both by the symmetric axiom: a square γ ∈ D(Δ^1×Δ^1) is cartesian iff it is cocartesian. This is precisely the stability axiom for derivators. The page thus shows the motivation: the Mayer–Vietoris square for cohomology of a homotopy pushout is always a pullback, and asking it to be a pushout as well is what makes cohomology behave 'linearly', i.e. triangulated or stable.
errors: No real mathematical error. The identifications γ(0,1) ≃ H(X_a,ξ) etc. silently use that fibre ↪ preimage-of-slice is a cohomological equivalence for cofibred (or 'proper') φ. This is true, but is exactly what the hypothesis buys.

The provisional Der 6 as stated here only concerns squares of the special form K_*φ_*ξ, so it is weaker than the symmetric axiom of p.49. In an unpointed derivator, demanding cocartesianness of these squares already forces strong stability-type consequences. Grothendieck does not yet discuss pointedness here.
The claim that cocartesianness is not deducible from Der1–Der5 is correct, though not proved on the page. Non-stable derivators, e.g. that of spaces/simplicial sets, give counterexamples.

ideas.what: Cohomology with coefficients of the Grothendieck construction of a span is computed by K_*φ_*, giving a cartesian Mayer–Vietoris square H(𝒳) → H(X_a), H(X_b) → H(X_0) in any derivator
ideas.modern_name: homotopy-limit Mayer–Vietoris / Grothendieck construction as hocolim (Thomason) plus Kan extension calculus in derivators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason (1979) for the hocolim–Grothendieck construction; Heller, Franke, Maltsiniotis, Groth for derivator Kan-extension calculus
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (1990–91 manuscript) develops cofibred/proper base change; exact square not located

ideas.what: Use of strict inclusions of preimages of slices 𝒳_{/i} to replace a square commuting only up to 2-cell by a strictly commuting one with the same cohomology
ideas.modern_name: fibres vs homotopy fibres / comma-category replacement for (co)fibred functors (Quillen Theorem B style)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Quillen (1973); Grothendieck's 'smooth/proper' functors in Les Dérivateurs
ideas.where_published: Les Dérivateurs (proper/smooth functors), unsure of this precise use

ideas.what: Provisional axiom 'Der 6': for 𝒳 cofibred over the span, the cartesian square K_*φ_*ξ is also cocartesian; next page generalised to 'cartesian ⇔ cocartesian for all squares'
ideas.modern_name: stability axiom for (triangulated/stable) derivators; cf. Lurie HA 1.4.2.11 for ∞-categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Heller (stable homotopy theories, 1988/1997), Franke (1996), Keller, Maltsiniotis (triangulated derivators, 2001/2007), Groth (2013)
ideas.where_published: Possibly discussed in Les Dérivateurs; this early (≥1982) formulation in cote 105 notes is not published

ideas.what: Observation that the extra (co)cartesian condition is independent of Der1–Der5, and (next page) that the cofibred version for D and the fibred version for D° are not equivalent, leading to a self-dual axiom
ideas.modern_name: independence of stability from derivator axioms; self-duality of stable derivators (D stable ⇔ D^op stable)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in stable derivator theory (Groth, Maltsiniotis)

missed.claim: An early (from 1982) Grothendieck formulation of what is now the stability axiom for derivators. It is reached via a provisional 'Der 6' requiring the Mayer–Vietoris square of a cofibred category over a span to be both cartesian and cocartesian, then symmetrised on p.49 into 'cartesian iff cocartesian'. This documents that the stable/triangulated-derivator axiom, usually credited to Maltsiniotis/Franke/Heller/Groth, was formulated by Grothendieck in this form, with this motivation, well before Les Dérivateurs.
missed.quote: "Der 6" (provisoire) Si 𝒳 sur Ψ est cofibrant, ξ ... K_*φ_*(ξ) ∈ D(Q) ... cartésien, mais aussi ... cocartésien.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Attribution and history: shows the stability axiom arose from a Mayer–Vietoris/cofibration principle rather than from triangulated categories. It suggests an intermediate 'axiom des cofibrations', where only Grothendieck-construction squares are required bicartesian. Its relation to full stability, e.g. in non-pointed settings, does not appear to be studied.

missed.claim: The restricted axiom (only squares K_*φ_*ξ coming from cofibred categories over a span are required cocartesian) is formulated, then abandoned for the symmetric axiom. Whether it is genuinely weaker than stability, or forces pointedness/stability in general, is left open.
missed.quote: J'ai l'impression que ce n'est pas déductible des axiomes ... Der 1 - Der 5, 5'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A minor but well-posed question in derivator theory: characterise derivators satisfying Mayer–Vietoris-bicartesianness only for Grothendieck-construction squares.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (Kan extension of a span, Mayer–Vietoris, bicartesian squares) is standard today. Historically, though, it records Grothendieck around 1982 isolating the stability axiom for derivators, motivated by cohomology of cofibred categories. That axiom is normally credited to later authors, though its presence in Les Dérivateurs is uncertain.
transcription_corrections: 'X/_a, X/_0, X/_b' should be read as 𝒳_{/a}, 𝒳_{/0}, 𝒳_{/b}: preimages under φ of the slices of Ψ, which form a strictly commuting square of inclusions.
The NB line says the fibres X_a, X_b are disjoint in 𝒳, so the square X_0→X_a→𝒳, X_0→X_b→𝒳 is NOT commutative (only up to 2-cell). This contrasts with the following 'Mais ... est commutatif'.
'Ça serait le cas pour tout et. [?] 𝒳 propre' should be read roughly as 'Ça serait le cas pour 𝒳 propre au dessus de Ψ, sans avoir à le supposer cofibrant'.
'doit donner à coup sûr le contexte suppl.' is probably 'doit donner dans ce cas la condition suppl. qu'il est aussi cocartésien'.
In Der 6 the composite is written ψ = (𝒳 →φ Ψ →K Q), with Q annotated as Δ^1×Δ^1. The object is K_*φ_*(ξ) ∈ D(Q), which is said to be cartesian and also cocartesian.
Vertical marginal text beside Der 6 is a largely illegible inserted condition. The bottom right reads 'Axiome des cofibrations', with a note referring to Der 6.
